as_of: Sep 10, 2026 Asia-morning preview — US closed lower Wed Sep 9 (Dow -0.77%, S&P -0.48%, Nasdaq -0.64%) as Brent surged above $101 on escalating US-Iran tanker strikes; Nikkei -0.90%, KOSPI -2%, Europe sharply lower (DAX -1.66%, CAC -1.94%); US 10Y at 4.834% after weak auction; gold $4,457

dow_jones.note: Dow closed 52,380.66 Wed Sep 9, -0.77% (~-405 pts) — second straight down day as Brent broke above $101 on fresh US-Iran tanker escalation. Oil-led inflation/hawkish-Fed pressure persists; index remains ~1.2% below its pre-Labor-Day level.

sp500.note: S&P 500 closed 7,636.36, -0.48% (-37.16). Energy names bid on crude >$100 but the broader tape weighed by rates (10Y 4.834% after a soft $39B auction) and Mideast risk. Losses broad but orderly.

nasdaq.note: Nasdaq closed 26,253.34, -0.64% (-168.07). Tech gave back more than the S&P as yields near multi-decade highs pressured long-duration growth; AI/chip names led the downside after Tuesday's Qualcomm-Amazon pop faded.

us_markets.note: US CASH CLOSE Wed Sep 9: Dow -0.77%, S&P -0.48%, Nasdaq -0.64% — a second consecutive risk-off session as Brent pushed past $101 and the 10Y auction tailed (4.834%). Yields at/near two-decade highs keep equities capped into the Asia open.

hang_seng.note: HSI reference 25,274.96 (-0.17%) into the Sep 10 HK open. The index is tracking the overnight US/Europe risk-off, with oil/energy names likely to outperform on the crude spike while tech/semis stay soft. Watch the $101 Brent and the 4.83% US 10Y as the dual cross-market drivers.

hscei.note: HSCEI reference 8,369.05 into the open; mainland-H names likely the relative laggard, tracking A-share futures down ~0.4%.

hstech.note: Hang Seng TECH reference 4,420.79; regional semis/AI soft as US Nasdaq fell -0.64% and yields rose — HK tech faces headwinds into the open.

hong_kong.note: HK opens Sep 10 against an overnight backdrop of falling US/Europe equities (DAX -1.66%, CAC -1.94%), Brent above $101 on US-Iran tanker strikes, and Nikkei -0.90% / KOSPI -2% in Asia.

nikkei225.note: Nikkei 225 44,946.64 (-0.90%) — pressured by the global oil/rates risk-off and yen firmness; JGB 20Y yield +3bp to 3.73%, 30Y +3bp to 3.985% as long-end pressure builds.

kospi.note: KOSPI down as much as 2% intraday Sep 10 — Asia's worst major index, hit hardest by the tech/semis selloff and oil-led risk-off; a key regional risk gauge into the session.

ftse_china_a50_futures.note: FTSE China A50 futures opened -0.42% Sep 10, pointing to a soft A-share open as investors weigh the global risk-off and Brent >$100.

asia_pacific.note: Asia-Pacific Sep 10: broad risk-off. Nikkei -0.90%, KOSPI -2%, TSEC weighted opened -0.1%, A50 futures -0.42%. Oil >$100 and rising long-end yields (JGB 20Y 3.73%) are the dominant regional drivers.

ftse100.note: UK FTSE 100 -1.31% — energy strength on crude outweighed by broad risk-off and inflation/rates worries.

dax.note: German DAX -1.66% — among the worst-hit, with autos (US-EU tariff/trade friction, Chinese competition) and rate-sensitive names leading losses.

cac40.note: French CAC 40 -1.94% — weakest major European index, dragged by luxury/autos and the broad risk-off; German 10Y set for highest-yield issuance since 2010.

europe.note: Europe closed sharply lower Wed Sep 9: FTSE -1.31%, DAX -1.66%, CAC -1.94% — oil-led inflation fears, soft long-end bond markets (German 10Y issuance at 2010-high yields) and US-Canada/US-EU trade friction drove the selloff.

btc.note: BTC data not refreshed this cycle (crypto API via proxy unavailable at capture time); macro backdrop remains risk-off with Brent >$100 — crypto likely tracking the broader risk-asset softness.

eth.note: ETH not refreshed this cycle; direction contingent on Mideast headlines, crude, and the Fed path.

crypto.note: Crypto quote feed unavailable overnight (international API reachable only via proxy, which was offline during this capture). Data gap flagged rather than estimated.

brent_crude.note: Brent crude ABOVE $101 (last ~$101.59-101.62 at 01:16 UTC Sep 10), extending the move from ~$99-100 as US-Iran tanker escalation deepened — the single largest cross-market driver into the Asia session.

wti_crude.note: WTI ~$96.72 (+0.53%), fresh multi-week high; the prompt contract holds just under the psychological $97-100 zone as tanker strikes sustain the supply-risk premium.

gold.note: COMEX gold ~$4,457 (-0.18%), Singapore 沪金 955.0 (+0.51%). Report of 'gold fleeing the US' on weakening US-EU trust; safe-haven bid with momentum still constructive despite the small pullback.

silver_cn.note: Shanghai silver 沪银 +1.71% — industrial+monetary demand and the gold bid spillover.

copper_cn.note: Shanghai copper 沪铜 +0.62%; CITIC sees annual copper potentially reaching $16,000/t — supply-tightness narrative intact.

rebar_cn.note: Shanghai rebar 螺纹 -0.57% — construction demand soft; property/现房销售 reform in focus.

commodities.note: Energy is the standout: Brent >$101, WTI ~$96.7 on the US-Iran tanker strikes. Precious metals firm (gold ~$4,457, 沪银 +1.71%), base metals mixed-to-firm (沪铜 +0.62%), ferrous soft (螺纹 -0.57%).

macro.oil_iran_escalation: CRITICAL: US-Iran escalation persists — follow-through to the five Iranian oil tankers destroyed after an attempted attack on a US warship. White House officials said the US-Iran conflict may last through the remainder of Trump's term. Brent pushed above $101, WTI ~$96.7 — the dominant global market driver.
macro.us_treasury_10y_auction: $39B 10-year auction tailed: high yield 4.834%, bid-to-cover 2.71. US 10Y yields ~4.83%, at/near two-decade highs; 2Y +2bp to 4.42%. Weak long-end demand + 'new bond king' warning that a non-hike Fed invites fresh Treasury selling.
macro.treasury_buyback_disappointment: US Treasury announced a long-bond buyback cap of $6B with operations showing at least $4B — 'disappointment engulfed the market'; long-end yields rose further on the news.
macro.japan_jgb_pressure: JGB long end under pressure: 20Y yield +3bp to 3.73%, 30Y +3bp to 3.985%; Fitch noted rising JGB yields may keep more Japanese capital at home (a global duration/FX headwind).
macro.asia_market_open: Sep 10 Asia open: KOSPI -2% (worst), Nikkei -0.90%, TSEC opened -0.1%, FTSE China A50 futures -0.42%. Broad risk-off on oil >$100 + rising global long-end yields.
macro.us_cash_close_recap: US cash markets closed lower Wed Sep 9: Dow -0.77%, S&P -0.48%, Nasdaq -0.64% — second straight down session; Europe fell harder (DAX -1.66%, CAC -1.94%).
macro.china_a_pre_market: A-share pre-open Sep 10: 上证参考 3,950.02 / 深证 13,723.32 / 创业板 3,354.97; 沪深300 4,570.32. Margin financing balance fell ¥3.19B; A50 futures -0.42% point to a soft open. Aug China CPI/PPI both returned to positive — 'economy showing signs of repair'. 央行 7-day reverse repo was zero on Sep 9.
macro.fed_hike_watch: Hawkish repricing intact: blowout Aug payrolls + oil >$100 keep 'will the Fed hike again?' alive. September Fed path and the near-two-decade-high 10Y remain the key equity headwind.
macro.september_watch: For the Sep 10 Asia session: 1) Brent >$101 & US-Iran escalation (White House: could last through Trump's term); 2) rising long-end yields globally (US 10Y 4.834%, JGB 20Y 3.73%, German 10Y at 2010-high issuance); 3) KOSPI -2% tech lead-loss; 4) A50 futures -0.42% / China CPI-PPI back positive; 5) gold >$4,450 on US-EU trust erosion; 6) US-Canada tariff fray.
